Local operators must continue to leverage technological innovations and adapt to the robust growth projected in global mining services and industrial explosives to secure their competitive standing in the years ahead. Between 2020 and 2023, South African drill and blast companies operated within a dynamic sector marked by both expansion and advancements in technology, heavily influencing the competitive dynamics and market intelligence requirements for entities such as Veralogix Drilling & Blasting [12] . During this period, the industry witnessed a structural shift toward integrating advanced technological solutions to meet the rigorous demands of various mining sectors. The service scope of leading South African drill-and-blast companies between 2020 and 2023 was primarily characterized by an emphasis on operational efficiency, safety, and technological integration. Brauteseth Blasting emerged as a notable player during this period, expanding its footprint across South Africa with the support of advanced drill rigs supplied by Sandvik Mining and Rock Solutions [12] . Such acquisitions highlight how service scope is intrinsically linked to the technological capabilities of the machinery deployed. For instance, the transition from surface quarrying to deep-level hard rock mining requires significant adjustments in both equipment and expertise. Companies must demonstrate agility in their service adaptation, utilizing advanced drill rigs and specialized blasting management techniques to optimize fragmentation while minimizing environmental impact and operational hazards. This adaptability is critical for companies seeking to secure long-term contracts across multiple mining sectors. The necessity for specialized expertise in executing these adapted services is reflected in the sector's labor dynamics. Recent job advertisements and recruitment materials from platforms like Indeed and Facebook highlight the ongoing need for specialized personnel. For example, Pioneer Drill Blast’s call for applications reflects the present demand for skilled roles in blasting management [14] [15] .
